To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the waist circumference (WC), a marker of central obesity, is a useful tool for identifying subjects at high risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a Colombian population.
a WC cut-off point lower than 94 cm is associated with the presence of CVRF in a sample of Colombian men.
the waist circumference cut-off point of ≥94 cm, which has been recommended in Caucasians to identify subjects with cardiovascular risk factors, is not valid in Colombian men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cardiovascular risk factors in a sample of Colombian subjects.
the development of a new method of analysis of the cardiovascular system.

the study of cardiovascular risk factors in a population of healthy men, and the determination of the cut-off points of waist circumference to identify subjects at high risk of developing cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WC value of <94 cm suggested in Caucasian populations is a poor screening tool for CVRF in our Colombian sample and the WC cut-off point value of 88 cm should be considered in this population.
the waist circumference (WC), a simple and noninvasive measure, is a good tool for identifying Colombian men at risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) when a WC cut-off point value of 88 cm is used.
the WC value for screening of cardiovascular risk factors is different for different ethnic groups, and it is not the same for all ethnic groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the waist circumference cut-off point of <88 cm in Colombian men is a better screening tool to identify subjects at cardiovascular risk than the 94-cm cut-off point recommended in Caucasians.
the cut-off point of the WC of 88 cm is more accurate in the Colombian population to identify subjects with CVFR.

waist circumference (WC), as a measure of central obesity, has a better diagnostic value in identifying subjects with cardiovascular risk factors than BMI, especially in populations with a higher prevalence of abdominal fat accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
waist circumference (WC), a simple and noninvasive measure of body fat, may be a useful tool to screen Colombian subjects at cardiovascular risk.

we have shown that the cut-off points for waist circumference to identify individuals at risk for cardiovascular disease are lower in our Latin American population than in the Caucasian population, which is in agreement with the results of previous studies in other ethnic groups.
we need to consider ethnic background when using WC as an index of cardiovascular risk.
